gym.name: Incline dumbbell or barbell press
gym.notes: 45° incline. Control the eccentric. Rest ~90–180s between sets
gym.where: Adjustable bench + dumbbells (or barbell / Smith incline). Bench about 30-45 degrees.
gym.how_to: Keep elbows moderately tucked and think about pressing the dumbbells up and back toward your face, rather than just straight up. Control the descent, slight pause, then press. Set the bench to about 30-45 degrees. Plant your feet flat. Pull your shoulder blades back into the pad. Start with the weights at upper-chest height, elbows about 45 degrees from your torso (not flared flat out). Press up until arms are almost straight without slamming. Lower for about 2 seconds until you feel a stretch across the upper chest.
gym.avoid: Bench too upright (turns into a shoulder press). Bouncing the bar/dumbbells off the chest. Huge arch and lifting the hips.
set_plan_lines: Set 1: pick X kg for 8–10 reps stopping with 1–2 clean reps left (not failure)
Set 2: same X kg, or X + 2.5 kg if set 1 felt easy
Set 3: X + 2.5 kg only if form stayed smooth — else stay at X

rom_cues.question: Full stretch at the bottom?
rom_cues.answer: Yes — lower until you feel an upper-chest stretch (~2 sec). Do not bounce.
rom_cues.why: “Bring the dumbbells all the way down on presses until you feel a nice deep stretch in your pecs.” — How To Train For Pure Muscle Growth

tips: control the lowering - that stretch is where a lot of the chest work happens.
keep shoulder blades pinned; do not shrug into your ears.

gym.name: Seated dumbbell or machine shoulder press
gym.notes: Don't shrug. Full lockout without slamming. Rest ~90–180s between sets
gym.where: Seated bench with back support + dumbbells, or a shoulder-press machine.
gym.how_to: Leave 1–2 reps in the tank on free-weight presses. Machine is fine for a hard last set. Soft lockout — no shrug. Sit tall with your back against the pad. Start with dumbbells at about ear height. Press overhead until arms lock softly. Lower only to ear height or the machine start position; do not drop into a relaxed dead hang at the bottom. Do not shrug. On a machine: same path, slow and controlled.
gym.avoid: Big lower-back arch. Pressing the weights far out in front of your face. Dropping into a loose hang between reps.

rom_cues.question: Lower to a fully relaxed hang?
rom_cues.answer: No. Stop around ear height (or the machine’s start). Soft lockout at the top — no slam.
rom_cues.why: A dead hang dumps tension, stresses the shoulder joint, and turns the next rep into a risky heave. Controlled end-range keeps delts working.

tips: this builds the front and middle of the shoulder - key for that round look.
stop the set when form shakes; do not fight ugly reps in week 1.

gym.name: Dumbbell or cable side lateral raise
gym.notes: Visual priority — soft elbows, lead with elbows. Last set: 0–1 clean reps left — controlled, not a collapse. Rest ~60–90s
gym.where: Dumbbells standing, cable with a handle at your side, or a lateral-raise machine.
gym.how_to: Raise cable height so tension peaks when the cable and arm form ~90°. Stretch the cable across your body — don’t stop at your side. Resist the negative 2–4 seconds. Soft bend in the elbows. Lead with the elbows and raise arms out to just below shoulder height. Pause briefly. Lower slowly. Prefer clean reps over heavy weight - this is your main "wider shoulders" move.
gym.avoid: Swinging the body. Shrugging traps. Flinging weights above the head.
set_plan_lines: Set 1: light X kg (often 4–8) for 12–15 with ~2 left — stop with 1–2 clean reps left
Set 2: same X, or +2 / +2.5 kg if easy and strict
Set 3: stay strict — if you swing, the weight is too heavy

gym.name: Cable or machine chest fly
gym.notes: Squeeze at the inside; no ego weight. Rest ~60–90s
gym.where: Pec-deck / fly machine, or dual cables at chest height.
gym.how_to: Fixed elbow bend. Open to a chest stretch, hug together. If standing cables pull you around, lean forward and fly downward. Keep a slight bend in the elbows and keep that bend fixed. Open until you feel a chest stretch, then bring the arms together as if hugging a tree. Squeeze one second at the inside.

Set 2: same pin, or +1 pin if easy
Set 3: stay controlled — light is correct

gym.notes: Elbows pinned. Rest ~60–90s

effort_rule.question: How hard should you push?
effort_rule.headline: Jeff’s rule: last set to failure — earlier sets leave reps
effort_rule.easy_answer: Leave 1–2 reps in the tank on early sets. Last set — send it (especially machines/cables).
effort_rule.answer: Jeff: conflicting evidence on failure vs near-failure, so he leaves 1–2 early and takes the last set to failure so you learn what RIR feels like.
effort_rule.one_liner: Early sets 1–2 RIR · last set to failure · compounds keep a rep if free-weight heavy.
do: Do 2–3 hard sets on most exercises.
Earlier sets: leave one or two clean reps.
Last set: take it to failure (machines/cables preferred).
Heavy free-weight compounds: still leave a rep or two even on the last set.
Control a 2–4 second negative — especially near failure.
dont: Don’t fail every set of squats/bench/RDLs with ugly form.
Don’t rest under 1 minute as a default — Jeff: ≥1 min is generally better.
Don’t chase novelty every week — progress the same menu.
feel_checks: Last 2–3 reps should feel slow and demanding.
If you had 4+ easy reps left, go heavier next set.
If form breaks, the set is over.
Side delts / curls / flies / pushdowns: last set may be 0 RIR.

effort_rule.question: How hard should you push?
effort_rule.headline: Jeff’s rule: last set to failure — earlier sets leave reps
effort_rule.easy_answer: Leave 1–2 reps in the tank on early sets. Last set — send it (especially machines/cables).
effort_rule.answer: Jeff: conflicting evidence on failure vs near-failure, so he leaves 1–2 early and takes the last set to failure so you learn what RIR feels like.
effort_rule.one_liner: Early sets 1–2 RIR · last set to failure · compounds keep a rep if free-weight heavy.
do: Do 2–3 hard sets on most exercises.
Earlier sets: leave one or two clean reps.
Last set: take it to failure (machines/cables preferred).
Heavy free-weight compounds: still leave a rep or two even on the last set.
Control a 2–4 second negative — especially near failure.
dont: Don’t fail every set of squats/bench/RDLs with ugly form.
Don’t rest under 1 minute as a default — Jeff: ≥1 min is generally better.
Don’t chase novelty every week — progress the same menu.
feel_checks: Last 2–3 reps should feel slow and demanding.
If you had 4+ easy reps left, go heavier next set.
If form breaks, the set is over.
Side delts / curls / flies / pushdowns: last set may be 0 RIR.
